editor_note: None of the 7 rewritten entries changes the meaning. Retirement dates, the 5x EPLG and 8x gate-speed figures, the 75x Gen3 speedup, the On-Prem Plan exception and the incompatibility note are all kept. There are two small problems. Entry 180 uses 'sirkuit yang lebih berperforma', but the rest of the file keeps 'circuit' (for example 'desain circuit' and 'Grafik pewaktuan circuit'), and 'lebih berperforma' is stiff. Entry 272 has calqued phrasing: 'pada satu QPU dalam satu waktu' and the redundant 'sebagian persentase job'.

examples.source: leading to more performant circuits
examples.translation: yang menghasilkan sirkuit yang lebih berperforma
examples.suggested: sehingga performa circuit menjadi lebih baik
examples.why: The rest of the file keeps 'circuit' in English, so 'sirkuit' here is inconsistent. 'lebih berperforma' is also a stiff calque.

examples.source: The rollout will be done on one QPU at a time, where a percentage of the jobs on the QPU will use the Gen3 path.
examples.translation: Peluncuran akan dilakukan pada satu QPU dalam satu waktu, di mana sebagian persentase job pada QPU tersebut akan menggunakan jalur Gen3.
examples.suggested: Peluncuran akan dilakukan satu per satu QPU, dan sebagian job pada QPU tersebut akan menggunakan jalur Gen3.
examples.why: 'dalam satu waktu' is a word-for-word copy of 'at a time', and 'sebagian persentase' says the same thing twice. The meaning is still correct.

editor_note: I checked all six rewritten entries (4, 7, 11, 22, 26, 30) against the English and none of them changes the meaning or would mislead a learner. There are three small problems. Entry 22 contains the malformed plural "qubit-Qubit Backend tersebut", where "qubit Backend tersebut" is the natural wording. Entry 26 says "melakukan Transpile Circuit kuantum" and then "sebuah sirkuit" in the same sentence, while entry 7 uses "melakukan transpilasi sirkuit kuantum", so the page uses two different renderings for transpile and for circuit. Entry 30's in-page link text is still the English "Visualize backends", but the heading it points to (entry 21) was translated as "Visualisasikan backend".

examples.source: as well as how a circuit is laid out across the qubits of a backend
examples.translation: serta bagaimana sebuah sirkuit ditata di atas qubit-Qubit Backend tersebut
examples.suggested: serta bagaimana sebuah sirkuit ditata pada qubit-qubit backend tersebut
examples.why: The reduplicated plural mixes capitalization ('qubit-Qubit'), which is malformed. A plain 'qubit' or 'qubit-qubit' reads naturally.

examples.source: it is straightforward to transpile quantum circuits against this backend
examples.translation: cukup mudah untuk melakukan Transpile Circuit kuantum terhadap Backend ini
examples.suggested: cukup mudah untuk melakukan transpilasi sirkuit kuantum terhadap backend ini
examples.why: Entry 7 renders this as 'melakukan transpilasi sirkuit', and later in this same sentence the page switches to 'sebuah sirkuit'. Mixing 'Transpile Circuit' with 'transpilasi sirkuit' is inconsistent.

examples.source: using the functions from the [Visualize backends](#visualize-backends) section
examples.translation: menggunakan fungsi-fungsi dari bagian [Visualize backends](#visualize-backends)
examples.suggested: menggunakan fungsi-fungsi dari bagian [Visualisasikan backend](#visualize-backends)
examples.why: The link text should match the translated heading (entry 21) so the learner can find the section it refers to.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The resilience-level trade-off, the beta caveat, the override note (level 0 plus zne_mitigation = True) and the level-2 example (ZNE, TREX, gate twirling) all match the English, so nothing here would mislead a learner. The main defect is that the informal register switches back and forth: "hasilmu"/"jobmu"/"Kamu bisa" sit next to "Anda bisa"/"Anda tentukan", and entry [24] switches from "Kamu" to "Anda" inside a single sentence. Smaller slips: [22] renders circuit two ways in one phrase ("dari satu sirkuit ke Circuit lainnya"), and [20] reorders "TREX measurement twirling" into the slightly awkward "Pengukuran twirling TREX".

examples.source: You can use resilience levels to specify noise management techniques, or you can set custom techniques individually
examples.translation: Kamu bisa menggunakan level resilience ... atau Anda bisa mengatur teknik kustom secara individual
examples.suggested: Kamu bisa menggunakan level resilience ... atau kamu bisa mengatur teknik kustom secara individual
examples.why: The pronoun changes from kamu to Anda within one sentence, and the file overall mixes -mu/kamu (entries [6], [31], [37]) with Anda (entries [18], [25]). Pick one form and use it throughout.

examples.source: will vary from circuit to circuit
examples.translation: akan bervariasi dari satu sirkuit ke Circuit lainnya
examples.suggested: akan bervariasi dari satu sirkuit ke sirkuit lainnya
examples.why: The same noun is written two ways in one idiom (lowercase Indonesian 'sirkuit', then capitalized English 'Circuit'), which reads as a glitch.

examples.source: Twirled Readout Error eXtinction (TREX) measurement twirling
examples.translation: Pengukuran twirling [Twirled Readout Error eXtinction (TREX)]
examples.suggested: Twirling pengukuran [Twirled Readout Error eXtinction (TREX)]
examples.why: The technique is twirling applied to measurements, so 'twirling pengukuran' is the natural head-modifier order. 'Pengukuran twirling' reads like 'twirling measurement'.

editor_note: None of the five rewritten entries (38, 45, 56, 58, 60) would mislead a learner. The fake_provider caveat in entry 45 ("hanya memungkinkan untuk Circuit kecil") is kept, and so is the resilience-level trade-off in entry 60. The remaining issues are stylistic. Entries 38, 45 and 58 switch between formal "Anda" and informal "-mu" inside a single sentence ("Ini mengharuskan Anda sudah menyimpan kredensialmu", "Saat Anda menjalankan program kuantummu ... beban kerjamu"). Entry 56 also turns the English hypothetical ("would reveal the level of noise") into a flat prediction ("akan semakin tidak akurat, dan itu menunjukkan..."), which slightly shifts it from how to diagnose noise to what will happen. It is not misleading, because entry 62 confirms that the signal does decay.

examples.source: It requires that you have already [saved your credentials]
examples.translation: Ini mengharuskan Anda sudah [menyimpan kredensialmu]
examples.suggested: Ini mengharuskan Anda sudah [menyimpan kredensial Anda]
examples.why: The sentence mixes formal Anda with the informal -mu suffix, which reads unevenly to a native editor. Entry 58 has the same problem.

examples.source: When you run your quantum program on a real device, your workload must wait in a queue
examples.translation: Saat Anda menjalankan program kuantummu di perangkat nyata, beban kerjamu harus menunggu dalam antrian
examples.suggested: Saat Anda menjalankan program kuantum di perangkat nyata, beban kerja Anda harus menunggu dalam antrean
examples.why: Anda and -mu are mixed in the same sentence. Also, 'antrean' is the standard KBBI spelling, not 'antrian'.

examples.source: Increasingly inaccurate (corrupted) expectation values between distant qubits would reveal the level of noise present.
examples.translation: Nilai ekspektasi antar-qubit yang berjauhan akan semakin tidak akurat (rusak), dan itu menunjukkan tingkat noise yang ada.
examples.suggested: Nilai ekspektasi antar-qubit berjauhan yang semakin tidak akurat (rusak) akan mengungkap tingkat noise yang ada.
examples.why: The English is a hypothetical about how to diagnose noise, but the translation states a prediction. The claim gets slightly stronger and the sentence is split into two clauses joined by 'dan itu'.

editor_note: None of the four rewritten entries (9, 14, 17, 21) changes the meaning, so nothing here would mislead a learner. Entry 21 leaves the English word "bespoke" untranslated ("konstruksi Circuit bespoke"), which an Indonesian reader would not expect; "yang dirancang khusus" is the natural wording. Entry 17 opens with the stiff calque "Langkah ini melibatkan menjalankan …" and uses "antrian", where KBBI spells it "antrean". Entries 9 and 14 are faithful and read naturally.

examples.source: from bespoke circuit construction to utility-scale workflows
examples.translation: dari konstruksi Circuit bespoke ke alur kerja skala utilitas
examples.suggested: dari konstruksi Circuit yang dirancang khusus ke alur kerja skala utilitas
examples.why: 'bespoke' is an English word Indonesian technical writers would not leave untranslated, and it is not a domain term.

examples.source: This step involves running your circuits on hardware
examples.translation: Langkah ini melibatkan menjalankan Circuit-mu pada perangkat keras
examples.suggested: Pada langkah ini, kamu menjalankan Circuit-mu pada perangkat keras
examples.why: Putting a verb straight after 'melibatkan' copies the English '-ing' structure and reads stiffly.

examples.source: without queuing delays
examples.translation: tanpa penundaan antrian
examples.suggested: tanpa penundaan antrean
examples.why: 'antrean' is the standard KBBI spelling; 'antrian' is the non-standard variant.

editor_note: None of the four rewritten entries misleads a learner. Entries 8 and 9 are faithful. In entry 4, "the sum of noise factors" became "jumlah faktor derau". In the same sentence, "Jumlah Gate dua-Qubit" means "the number of", so a reader could take it as the count of noise factors rather than their sum. "total faktor derau" or "hasil penjumlahan faktor derau" would remove that doubt. Entry 3 adds something the English doesn't say: that the job is first "dikirim ke layanan validasi job". The English only says the job "is first validated". The addition matches the page description, so it isn't a false claim, but it goes beyond the source.

examples.source: The number of two-qubit gates is multiplied by the sum of noise factors requested in gate-folding ZNE.
examples.translation: Jumlah Gate dua-Qubit dikalikan dengan jumlah faktor derau (noise factor) yang diminta dalam gate-folding ZNE.
examples.suggested: Jumlah Gate dua-Qubit dikalikan dengan total faktor derau (noise factor) yang diminta dalam gate-folding ZNE.
examples.why: Here "jumlah" appears twice, first meaning "number of" and then "sum". A reader could take the multiplier as the count of noise factors rather than their sum, so "total" makes it clear.

examples.source: it is first validated to try to ensure that the job can run on the QPU
examples.translation: job tersebut pertama-tama dikirim ke layanan validasi job. Layanan ini berusaha memastikan bahwa job dapat berjalan di QPU
examples.suggested: job tersebut pertama-tama divalidasi untuk memastikan bahwa job dapat berjalan di QPU
examples.why: The English doesn't say the job is sent to a validation service; it only says the job is validated. The addition matches the page description, so it isn't false, but it goes beyond the source.

editor_note: None of the five rewritten entries (2, 11, 16, 28, 31) would mislead a learner. The meaning is faithful: noise-model behaviour, circuit-size limits, runtime comparisons and use cases in the table all match the English, and entry 31 keeps the claim that the snapshot noise model is applied automatically. The one thing to fix is the header row of the entry 28 table. It is left entirely in English, so "Clifford Simulation" appears there while the section heading in entry 40 and the body text use "Simulasi Clifford". The rest of the table is translated, which makes the header row look overlooked.

examples.source: | Simulator | Fake Backends | AerSimulator | Clifford Simulation |
examples.translation: | Simulator | Fake Backends | AerSimulator | Clifford Simulation |
examples.suggested: | Simulator | Fake backend | AerSimulator | Simulasi Clifford |
examples.why: The header row was left in English, but every other row of the table is translated. The page itself renders the concept as 'Simulasi Clifford' (entry 40) and uses 'fake backend' in lowercase in the body text (entries 29, 31).

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The twirling precedence rule, the job-splitting example [A, C]@0.01 / [B]@0.05, the Batch submit-all-then-collect warning and the ConvertISAToClifford caveats all match the source, and nothing would mislead a learner. What a native editor would change is style. A few phrasings are stiff calques: "Circuit Clifford bersimulasi secara efisien" [53], "tata letakkan observable" [55] and "Parameter di-bind sepenuhnya" [56]. "Options" is also used inconsistently: the English word appears in "objek options", "Pohon options" and "Kelas options", while "opsi" is used elsewhere ("opsi input", "jalur opsi").

examples.source: Clifford circuits simulate efficiently (stabilizer simulation) regardless of size.
examples.translation: Circuit Clifford bersimulasi secara efisien (simulasi stabilizer) terlepas dari ukurannya.
examples.suggested: Circuit Clifford dapat disimulasikan secara efisien (simulasi stabilizer) berapa pun ukurannya.
examples.why: The circuit is what gets simulated, so the sentence needs the passive form. The active 'bersimulasi' is a calque of the English.

examples.source: Lay the observable out from the **pre-Clifford ISA** circuit instead
examples.translation: Sebagai gantinya, tata letakkan observable dari circuit ISA **sebelum-Clifford**
examples.suggested: Sebagai gantinya, terapkan layout pada observable berdasarkan circuit ISA **sebelum Cliffordisasi**
examples.why: 'tata letakkan' is an awkward verb form. Using 'layout' fits apply_layout and reads more naturally.

examples.source: **Parameters are bound away.**
examples.translation: **Parameter di-bind sepenuhnya.**
examples.suggested: **Parameter hilang karena sudah terikat ke nilai tetap.**
examples.why: The English idiom is carried over literally. The source means the parameters no longer exist after rounding, and 'di-bind sepenuhnya' does not say that clearly.

examples.source: if you construct typed options objects
examples.translation: jika kamu membuat objek options bertipe
examples.suggested: jika kamu membuat objek opsi bertipe
examples.why: The English 'options' is kept here and in 'Pohon options' [17] and 'Kelas options' [20/22], but the same text also uses 'opsi' ('opsi input', 'jalur opsi'). The file should use one term.

editor_note: None of the 9 rewritten entries misleads a learner. The server-side/client-side split in [8] ("EstimatorV2 sisi server" vs "Estimator sisi klien yang baru"), the version numbers and the uniform_modification explanation in [31] all match the English. One small inconsistency: [31] translates "equivalent boxes" as "box ekuivalen", but [32], which explains why the refs differ ("since they are not equivalent"), uses "setara". That breaks the lexical link between the rule and its example. Using "ekuivalen" in both places would keep the reasoning visible.

examples.source: two of which contain `InjectNoise` annotations with different `ref` attributes (since they are not equivalent).
examples.translation: dua di antaranya mengandung anotasi `InjectNoise` dengan atribut `ref` yang berbeda (karena tidak setara).
examples.suggested: dua di antaranya mengandung anotasi `InjectNoise` dengan atribut `ref` yang berbeda (karena tidak ekuivalen).
examples.why: Entry [31] states the rule for 'box ekuivalen'. Using 'setara' here hides that this sentence applies the same rule, so the reader can miss the connection.

editor_note: Entries 4-6 are faithful and natural. "Activity tracking events" becomes "event pelacakan aktivitas", "route" becomes "merutekan" and "alert on events" becomes "memberi peringatan pada event", all used consistently, and the audit-compliance clause and routing-target caveat are kept intact.

The meaning is faithful all the way through, and nothing would mislead a learner. The QAOA explanation, the benchmark caveats (such as the 90/100-qubit noise degradation) and the binary-to-spin mapping example all match the source. There are a few style problems. "Qiskit Function" is rendered as "Fungsi Qiskit" in [1], [35] and [56] but left as "Qiskit Function" / "function ini" in [62]. "Disclaimer" becomes "Penyangkalan", which is an odd choice ("Penafian" is the usual word). A few lines are calqued: "Mencetak hasil memberikan hasil berikut" [46], "Panduan pengguna memulai" [58], and "pertama kali didefinisikan" [37], where the source means "first, define".

examples.source: Request access to the function ... for this Qiskit Function.
examples.translation: Minta akses ke function ini ... untuk Qiskit Function ini.
examples.suggested: Minta akses ke fungsi ini ... untuk Fungsi Qiskit ini.
examples.why: Entries [1], [35] and [56] use "Fungsi Qiskit", so this entry is inconsistent with the rest of the file.

examples.source: title="Disclaimer"
examples.translation: title="Penyangkalan"
examples.suggested: title="Penafian"
examples.why: "Penyangkalan" means denial or refutation. The usual Indonesian word for a disclaimer is "Penafian".

examples.source: Printing the results gives the following:
examples.translation: Mencetak hasil memberikan hasil berikut:
examples.suggested: Hasil cetaknya adalah sebagai berikut:
examples.why: "hasil" is repeated, and the sentence is a word-for-word calque of the English.

examples.source: The problem is first defined by using a dictionary:
examples.translation: Masalah ini pertama kali didefinisikan dengan menggunakan dictionary:
examples.suggested: Pertama, masalah didefinisikan terlebih dahulu menggunakan dictionary:
examples.why: "pertama kali" means "for the first time". The source means "first" as a step in a sequence, which is "terlebih dahulu".

examples.source: Getting started user guide.
examples.translation: Panduan pengguna memulai.
examples.suggested: Panduan memulai untuk pengguna.
examples.why: The word order is calqued from English and reads ungrammatically in Indonesian.

editor_note: None of the three rewritten entries would mislead a learner. In entry 20 the numbers (~44% vs ~95,3%, "puluhan mikrodetik", "rentang waktu yang sama") and the QED-alone vs QED+Orbit contrast match the English, and entry 22 keeps its caveat about device, calibration and settings. Two small wording slips remain. Entry 20 opens with the calque "Melihat ke depan menuju era toleransi kesalahan", which a native writer would phrase more idiomatically. Entry 61 renders "orbit-enabled custom DD strategies" as "strategi DD kustom di dalam Orbit", which moves the stress from "strategies Orbit enables" to "strategies located inside Orbit".

examples.source: Looking ahead to the era of fault tolerance, Orbit is also compatible with...
examples.translation: Melihat ke depan menuju era toleransi kesalahan, Orbit juga kompatibel dengan...
examples.suggested: Menyongsong era toleransi kesalahan, Orbit juga kompatibel dengan...
examples.why: 'Melihat ke depan menuju' is a literal calque of 'looking ahead to'. The meaning is intact, but it reads stiff.

examples.source: to learn how to define orbit-enabled custom DD strategies
examples.translation: untuk mempelajari cara mendefinisikan strategi DD kustom di dalam Orbit
examples.suggested: untuk mempelajari cara mendefinisikan strategi DD kustom yang didukung Orbit
examples.why: 'orbit-enabled' means Orbit makes these strategies possible. 'di dalam Orbit' says they live inside Orbit. The nuance shifts slightly, but a learner would not be misled.

editor_note: All four rewritten entries (5, 16, 20, 24) keep the English meaning and read naturally, e.g. "Argumen `generate_preset_pass_manager` sama dengan argumen fungsi `transpile`" and "Untuk melihat cara kerja pass manager ini, coba jalankan pada sirkuit dua qubit".

None of the six rewritten entries (7, 20, 34, 36, 38, 48) changes the meaning. In entry 48, X is still on the bottom and Y on the top. Entries 7 and 38 keep the left-to-right evaluation, and entry 36 keeps "a frequent source of confusion". Terminology matches the rest of the page (circuit, gate, qubit, kabel, masukan/keluaran). What remains is minor, calqued phrasing. Entry 34 "sangat penting bahwa kita terlebih dahulu" and "Ini terhubung dengan" copy the English word for word. Entry 7 "Aliran informasi ... mengalir" is redundant, and entry 48 ends on a stiff "adalah ini:".

examples.source: it is imperative that we first clarify how qubits are ordered ... This connects with the convention that Qiskit uses
examples.translation: sangat penting bahwa kita terlebih dahulu mengklarifikasi bagaimana qubit diurutkan ... Ini terhubung dengan konvensi yang digunakan Qiskit
examples.suggested: kita perlu terlebih dahulu memperjelas bagaimana qubit diurutkan ... Hal ini berkaitan dengan konvensi yang digunakan Qiskit
examples.why: Two word-for-word calques. 'sangat penting bahwa kita' copies 'it is imperative that we', and 'terhubung dengan' is the literal word for 'connects'; in Indonesian technical prose, 'berkaitan dengan' is the natural choice.

examples.source: The flow of information along the wires goes from left to right
examples.translation: Aliran informasi sepanjang kabel mengalir dari kiri ke kanan
examples.suggested: Informasi mengalir sepanjang kabel dari kiri ke kanan
examples.why: Redundant: 'aliran ... mengalir' says 'the flow flows'. The meaning is correct.

examples.source: the matrix representation of the controlled-NOT gate is this:
examples.translation: representasi matriks dari gate controlled-NOT adalah ini:
examples.suggested: representasi matriks gate controlled-NOT adalah sebagai berikut:
examples.why: 'adalah ini:' is a stiff calque of 'is this:'. Elsewhere the file introduces displays with 'sebagai berikut:'.

editor_note: All three rewritten entries (5, 29, 32) keep the English meaning. Nothing is inverted, dropped or added: the "infinitely many errors" setup, the "bit-flip, phase-flip, or both" condition, the list of channels and the Pauli linear combination all match. The one problem is that "arbitrary" becomes "sembarangan" ("kesalahan uniter satu qubit yang sembarangan", "kesalahan yang sembarangan", "kanal qubit sembarangan"). In everyday Indonesian "sembarangan" means careless or reckless, and the standard mathematical word is "sembarang" (or "sebarang"). In entry 29, "yang sembarangan yang tidak harus uniter" also stacks two "yang" clauses and reads stiffly.

examples.source: we will succeed in correcting an arbitrary single-qubit unitary error
examples.translation: berhasil mengoreksi kesalahan uniter satu qubit yang sembarangan
examples.suggested: berhasil mengoreksi kesalahan uniter sembarang pada satu qubit
examples.why: In Indonesian math writing, 'arbitrary' is 'sembarang'. 'Sembarangan' means careless or reckless, which is the wrong connotation here.

examples.source: let's consider arbitrary errors that are not necessarily unitary ... an arbitrary qubit channel $\Phi$
examples.translation: mari kita pertimbangkan kesalahan yang sembarangan yang tidak harus uniter ... kanal qubit sembarangan $\Phi$
examples.suggested: mari kita tinjau kesalahan sembarang yang belum tentu uniter ... kanal qubit sembarang $\Phi$
examples.why: Two 'yang' clauses in a row read stiffly. 'Belum tentu' is the natural way to say 'not necessarily', and it has the same 'sembarangan' vs 'sembarang' problem as entry 5.

editor_note: None of the three rewritten entries would mislead a learner, and entry 4 (fragility, isolation vs. control, the early pessimism) is faithful and natural. In entry 3, "yang belum ada algoritma klasik efisiennya, dan mungkin memang tidak ada" blurs the English contrast between "not known" and "possibly don't exist". "Belum ada" already means "doesn't exist yet", so the second clause adds nothing, and "belum diketahui" would restore the distinction. In entry 6, "melihat sekilas untuk pertama kalinya" is a stiff calque of "take a first look". "Sekilas" also suggests only a brief glance, while the lesson is really an introduction.

examples.source: for which efficient classical algorithms are not known, and possibly don't exist
examples.translation: yang belum ada algoritma klasik efisiennya, dan mungkin memang tidak ada
examples.suggested: yang algoritma klasik efisiennya belum diketahui, dan mungkin memang tidak ada
examples.why: 'Belum ada' means 'doesn't yet exist', so the contrast between 'not known' and 'may not exist' disappears. That distinction matters in complexity theory. This is minor because the overall claim still holds.

examples.source: we'll take a first look at quantum error correction
examples.translation: kita akan melihat sekilas untuk pertama kalinya koreksi kesalahan kuantum
examples.suggested: kita akan mulai berkenalan dengan koreksi kesalahan kuantum
examples.why: This is a word-for-word calque and reads stiffly. 'Sekilas' also suggests only a passing glance rather than an introductory treatment.

editor_note: Entry 17 keeps every clause of the Credly notice, with no drift or hedging: "pemroses data pihak ketiga yang diotorisasi oleh IBM", "IBM dapat berbagi … secara global" and "praktik privasi IBM" all match the English, and it stays in the page's informal "kamu/-mu" register.

I checked the three rewritten entries (3, 4 and 6) against the English, and none of them would mislead a learner. Entry 3 keeps the lower-bound point ("menyamai batas bawah yang sudah diketahui sebelumnya"), and entry 6 keeps the hedge ("mungkin belum ... dalam waktu dekat"). Entry 6 copies the English wording in "teknik ... yang menemukan banyak aplikasi" ("finds many applications"), which an Indonesian editor would change to "memiliki banyak aplikasi" or "banyak diterapkan". "Merupakan representasi dari" also reads stiffly. In entry 4, "berlaku secara luas" is a weaker fit for "broadly applicable" than "dapat diterapkan secara luas", and "terkadang dimungkinkan untuk" is wordy.

examples.source: it is representative of a more general technique that finds many applications in quantum algorithms
examples.translation: dan merupakan representasi dari teknik yang lebih umum yang menemukan banyak aplikasi dalam algoritma kuantum
examples.suggested: dan algoritma ini mewakili teknik yang lebih umum yang memiliki banyak aplikasi dalam algoritma kuantum
examples.why: 'menemukan banyak aplikasi' copies the English 'finds many applications' word for word. Indonesian says 'memiliki banyak aplikasi' or 'banyak diterapkan', and 'mewakili' is less stiff than 'merupakan representasi dari'.

examples.source: Grover's algorithm is also broadly applicable ... sometimes it's possible to use Grover's algorithm
examples.translation: Algoritma Grover juga berlaku secara luas ... terkadang dimungkinkan untuk menggunakan algoritma Grover
examples.suggested: Algoritma Grover juga dapat diterapkan secara luas ... terkadang algoritma Grover dapat digunakan bersama algoritma lain
examples.why: 'berlaku' means 'is valid' or 'holds', not 'is applicable'. 'dimungkinkan untuk menggunakan' is a wordy passive that reads like a translation.

editor_note: Entry 36 matches the English: "0 menunjukkan tidak ada optimisasi, dan 1 (default) menunjukkan beberapa optimisasi circuit ke perangkat keras yang dipilih" keeps the settings and the default, and the reason given for skip_transpilation ("karena kita sudah mentranspilasi circuit kita menggunakan pass manager") is intact.

None of the five rewritten entries (9, 49, 70, 115, 128) would mislead a learner. The ZNE steps, the Sampler/Estimator post-processing and the PEA plot description all match the English. Three wording problems remain. In entry 49, "resource demands are more modest" became "implementasinya tidak terlalu rumit" (implementation not too complicated), which drops the resource-cost framing that the sentence exists to make. In entry 128, "exact values/results" became "nilai tepat" and "hasil tepat", where "nilai eksak" is the usual technical term. In entry 9, "Judulnya terkenal ..." is a word-for-word calque of "famously titled".

examples.source: preparing initial states for which the implementation resource demands are more modest
examples.translation: mempersiapkan state awal yang implementasinya tidak terlalu rumit
examples.suggested: mempersiapkan state awal yang kebutuhan sumber daya implementasinya lebih ringan
examples.why: The English is about resource cost, not complexity, and the next sentence already covers complexity. The translation merges the two points into one.

examples.source: brings the results much closer to the exact values ... deviation from the exact results
examples.translation: jauh lebih dekat ke nilai tepat ... penyimpangan signifikan dari hasil tepat
examples.suggested: jauh lebih dekat ke nilai eksak ... penyimpangan signifikan dari hasil eksak
examples.why: In Indonesian physics writing, 'eksak' is the standard word for exact values. 'Tepat' reads more like 'accurate' or 'correct'.

examples.source: It was famously titled “There’s Plenty of Room at the Bottom,”
examples.translation: Judulnya terkenal "There's Plenty of Room at the Bottom,"
examples.suggested: Kuliah itu terkenal dengan judul "There's Plenty of Room at the Bottom,"
examples.why: This copies the English adverb structure word for word and reads stiffly. It can also be misread as 'its title is famous'.

editor_note: None of the five rewritten entries (7, 21, 83, 106, 109) would mislead a learner: the caveats, the exponential growth claim and the "32 bitstrings / four solutions in top five / two layers" facts all carry over. A native editor would still fix a few small things. In entry 7, "kemudian terapkan ini" has no subject and reads as an imperative, so it should be "kemudian menerapkannya". In entry 106, "memeriksa kewajarannya pada solusi" is clumsy. In entry 109, "setiap saat" ("at any moment") is used for "every time" and should be "setiap kali", and "solusi nyata" would be clearer as "solusi yang sebenarnya". In entry 21, "tumbuh secara eksponensial dalam jumlah simpul" is a calque of the English; "terhadap jumlah simpul" reads more naturally.

examples.source: then apply this to a utility-scale version of the problem
examples.translation: kemudian terapkan ini ke versi skala utilitas dari masalah tersebut
examples.suggested: kemudian menerapkannya ke versi skala utilitas dari masalah tersebut
examples.why: The verb has no subject and switches to the imperative in the middle of a 'kita akan' sentence, so it reads as a command to the reader.

examples.source: to sanity-check the solutions
examples.translation: untuk memeriksa kewajarannya pada solusi
examples.suggested: untuk memeriksa kewajaran solusinya
examples.why: The '-nya ... pada solusi' construction is awkward and repeats the reference to the solution.

examples.source: finding the best max-cut every time ... the four real solutions
examples.translation: menemukan Max-Cut terbaik setiap saat ... empat solusi nyata
examples.suggested: menemukan Max-Cut terbaik setiap kali ... empat solusi yang sebenarnya
examples.why: 'setiap saat' means 'at any moment', not 'on every run'. 'solusi nyata' could be read in the real-versus-complex sense; 'solusi yang sebenarnya' makes 'actual solutions' clear.

examples.source: grows exponentially in the number of nodes
examples.translation: tumbuh secara eksponensial dalam jumlah simpul
examples.suggested: tumbuh secara eksponensial terhadap jumlah simpul
examples.why: 'dalam' is a calque of the English 'in'. Indonesian technical writing normally uses 'terhadap' here.

editor_note: All three rewritten entries (29, 62 and 70) are faithful, and none of them would mislead a learner. Entry 29 keeps both the ket/column-vector convention and the caveat that the transpose has no numerical effect on NumPy 1D arrays. Entry 62 correctly says SQD suits wave functions where a small fraction of basis states have non-negligible amplitudes ("sebagian kecil ... amplitudo yang tidak dapat diabaikan"). The VQE/SQD table in entry 70 keeps every number (2951 terms, 1187 groups, 10^5-10^7 shots), the inverse dependence on sqrt(shots), and the upper-bound claim. The one slip is in entry 70: "can be restrictive" became "bisa sangat membatasi" ("can be very restrictive"). The added "sangat" slightly strengthens the claim, but not enough to mislead.

examples.source: For practical cases, this measurement overhead can be restrictive.
examples.translation: Untuk kasus praktis, overhead pengukuran ini bisa sangat membatasi.
examples.suggested: Untuk kasus praktis, overhead pengukuran ini bisa menjadi kendala.
examples.why: The added 'sangat' (very) makes the English 'can be restrictive' slightly stronger. This is minor and does not mislead, but a faithful rendering would leave out the intensifier.

editor_note: All three rewritten entries are faithful and natural: [38] keeps every property intact (persegi N×N, reversibel/invers, "tidak memperpanjang atau memperpendek vektor, tapi hanya merotasinya"), and [91] renders the interference analogy correctly as "saling memperkuat atau meniadakan".

Both rewritten entries keep the English meaning: 14 lessons, IBM Quantum with the University of Tokyo, the utility-scale goal and the Nature cover from June 2023 are all there. Entry 4 still has two calqued phrases. "Kursus replay acara ini" copies the English noun stack word for word and leaves "replay" untranslated. "difokuskan pada pembangunan menuju perhitungan skala utilitas" is a stiff noun phrase that no native technical writer would use. Entry 0's "kursus 14 pelajaran" is acceptable but would read better as "kursus berisi 14 pelajaran".

examples.source: This event replay course consists of 14 lessons and labs
examples.translation: Kursus replay acara ini terdiri dari 14 pelajaran dan lab
examples.suggested: Kursus ini, berupa rekaman ulang sebuah acara, terdiri dari 14 pelajaran dan lab
examples.why: It copies the English noun stack word for word and leaves 'replay' untranslated, so it reads as machine translation.

examples.source: but they are focused on building toward a utility-scale calculation
examples.translation: tetapi difokuskan pada pembangunan menuju perhitungan skala utilitas
examples.suggested: tetapi semuanya diarahkan untuk membangun sebuah perhitungan skala utilitas
examples.why: The noun phrase 'pembangunan menuju' is stiff, and 'pembangunan' suggests infrastructure development. A verb-based sentence reads more naturally.

editor_note: None of the 7 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. 'Algoritma kuantum variasional' (1, 3, 19), the 0/1 cut-membership caveat in 42 ('apakah node tersebut masuk dalam potongan atau tidak'), and the reason for using Sampler in 106 all keep the English meaning. The one thing a native editor would change is in entry 19: 'Gate yang mengambil parameter variasional' copies the English 'take parameters' word for word, and 'menerima parameter' is the natural Indonesian phrasing.

examples.source: we construct a circuit with gates that take variational parameters
examples.translation: kita membangun Circuit dengan Gate yang mengambil parameter variasional
examples.suggested: kita membangun Circuit dengan Gate yang menerima parameter variasional
examples.why: 'mengambil' (to take/fetch) is a literal copy of English 'take'. In Indonesian, a gate that accepts parameters is described with 'menerima'.

editor_note: All four rewritten entries (8, 23, 87, 127) keep their meaning; for example, entry 127 renders "ansatz circuit bound with the optimal parameters" as "Circuit ansatz yang telah diisi dengan parameter optimal", and entry 87's "Excited state" heading matches the term used throughout the page.

None of the three rewritten entries (21, 25, 27) changes the meaning. The sparsity condition, the P_S projector, the Jordan-Wigner-to-Fock-state logic and the every-4th-orbital (0, 4, 8) connectivity all match the English. Entry 21 has two wording problems. First, "classical post-processing block" becomes "blok pemrosesan ulang klasik", which reads as "reprocessing"; the standard term is "pascapemrosesan". Second, the same entry uses "himpunan" for S but "set" for X̃ a sentence later, so one mathematical notion gets two words. In entry 27, "Juga" for "Again" loses the sense that the heavy-hex topology is again the cause; "Lagi-lagi" or "Sama halnya" would keep it.

examples.source: passed into the classical post-processing block
examples.translation: dimasukkan ke blok pemrosesan ulang klasik
examples.suggested: dimasukkan ke blok pascapemrosesan klasik
examples.why: 'pemrosesan ulang' means reprocessing, not post-processing. The meaning is still recognizable, but the standard Indonesian term is 'pascapemrosesan'.

examples.source: a set of basis states S ... yielding the set of noisy configurations X̃ ... The set X̃
examples.translation: himpunan state basis S ... set konfigurasi berisik X̃ ... Set X̃
examples.suggested: himpunan konfigurasi berisik X̃ ... Himpunan X̃
examples.why: The same mathematical notion is rendered two ways within one paragraph. 'himpunan' is the right Indonesian term.

examples.source: Again, due to the heavy-hex topology,
examples.translation: Juga, karena topologi heavy-hex,
examples.suggested: Lagi-lagi, karena topologi heavy-hex,
examples.why: 'Juga' at the start of a sentence is stiff, and it drops the English point that the same topology is the cause a second time.

editor_note: I found nothing in the four rewritten entries (11, 16, 46, 49) that would mislead a learner. The Pauli-correction mapping (X on qubit 3, Z on qubit 0), the "over an order of magnitude" claim, the CDF axes and the "far-left = best" reading all match the English. The Bell state is named three ways across the delta: "keadaan Bell" in [16], "Bell state" in [49], and "state Bell" in the rest of the page. In [49], "at most that MSE" became "MSE paling banyak sebesar itu", which is awkward for a scalar threshold, and "ambang batas berkembang" is a stiff rendering of "threshold grows". In [16], "consumes that Bell pair" was flattened to "menggunakan", which loses the idea that the resource is used up.

examples.source: the fraction of qubit pairs that have at most that MSE on the y-axis
examples.translation: proporsi pasangan qubit yang memiliki MSE paling banyak sebesar itu pada sumbu-y
examples.suggested: proporsi pasangan qubit yang MSE-nya tidak melebihi nilai tersebut pada sumbu-y
examples.why: 'paling banyak' is used for counts, not for an error value. 'tidak melebihi' is the natural way to say 'at most' for a threshold.

examples.source: variation in Bell-state fidelity
examples.translation: variasi fidelitas Bell state
examples.suggested: variasi fidelitas state Bell
examples.why: The page uses 'state Bell' elsewhere, entry 16 uses 'keadaan Bell', and this entry uses the English word order 'Bell state'. That is three forms for one concept.

examples.source: a teleportation routine consumes that Bell pair to entangle qubits 0 and 3
examples.translation: rutinitas teleportasi menggunakan pasangan Bell tersebut untuk meng-entangle qubit 0 dan 3
examples.suggested: rutinitas teleportasi mengonsumsi pasangan Bell tersebut untuk meng-entangle qubit 0 dan 3
examples.why: 'consumes' tells the learner the Bell pair is used up by the protocol, which is a key LOCC idea. 'menggunakan' (uses) drops that.

editor_note: Nothing on this page would mislead a learner. The MIS constraint ("paling banyak satu endpoint"), the clique tightening, the pendant-node fixing and the fixed-angle QAOA and warm-start claims all keep their meaning. Terms are consistent throughout (kendala, suku penalti, optimisasi, sirkuit, transpilasi). A few spots are stiff or calqued. [19] copies "further reducing the effective problem size" word for word ("lebih lanjut mengurangi ukuran masalah efektif"). [67] uses the noun "Sampel" where the other list items use verbs. [18] "berbagi sebuah edge" reads like a calque of "shares an edge".

examples.source: further reducing the effective problem size
examples.translation: lebih lanjut mengurangi ukuran masalah efektif
examples.suggested: sehingga ukuran efektif masalah makin berkurang
examples.why: Copies the English participle clause word for word. Also, 'masalah efektif' makes 'efektif' describe the problem when it should describe the size.

examples.source: Sample from circuit with fixed parameters
examples.translation: Sampel dari sirkuit dengan parameter tetap
examples.suggested: Mengambil sampel dari sirkuit dengan parameter tetap
examples.why: This is a noun, while the other steps in the list are verbs (Mengurangi, Menemukan, Menerapkan). It reads as a fragment.

examples.source: every pair of nodes shares an edge
examples.translation: setiap pasangan node berbagi sebuah edge
examples.suggested: setiap pasangan node terhubung oleh sebuah edge
examples.why: 'berbagi sebuah edge' copies 'shares an edge'. 'terhubung oleh' is the usual phrasing in Indonesian graph theory, and entry [13] already uses it.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries are faithful and natural. In [59], "jumlah gate non-lokal (CZ dan RZZ untuk Backend ini)" and "nanti membandingkan" keep the deferred comparison. In [95], "metode translasi basis `constructor-beta`" is an accurate gloss, and "total jumlah gate berkurang" keeps the reduction claim.

The three rewritten entries are faithful and natural, e.g. [14] keeps every caveat ("Tidak ada memori antar pekerjaan", "sejumlah keuntungan", "menghindari masalah umum akibat perangkat mati di tengah eksekusi"), and [16] "Diagonalisasi kuantum berbasis sampel" matches [9].

None of the 14 rewritten titles drifts in meaning. Several of them break conventions that the rest of the page already uses. Entry 88 renders "error" as "error" ("Pembatalan error probabilistik"), while the page, including entry 84's identical phrase, uses "kesalahan" everywhere. Entry 18 keeps "ground state" in English although entry 32 uses "keadaan-dasar", and entry 45 keeps "workload" although the section heading and intro (entries 43-44) say "beban kerja". The adjacent titles in entries 58 and 59 also switch between the noun "Simulasi" and the imperative "Simulasikan".

examples.source: Probabilistic error cancellation with logical noise models
examples.translation: Pembatalan error probabilistik dengan model noise logis
examples.suggested: Pembatalan kesalahan probabilistik dengan model noise logis
examples.why: Everywhere else on the page 'error' is 'kesalahan', including entry 84's identical phrase 'Pembatalan kesalahan probabilistik'. The two PEC titles should match.

examples.source: SqDRIFT algorithm for ground state estimation
examples.translation: Algoritma SqDRIFT untuk estimasi ground state
examples.suggested: Algoritma SqDRIFT untuk estimasi keadaan dasar
examples.why: Entry 32 on the same page translates ground state as 'keadaan-dasar', so this title uses a different term for the same concept.

examples.source: Run quantum workloads with QRMI
examples.translation: Jalankan workload kuantum dengan QRMI
examples.suggested: Jalankan beban kerja kuantum dengan QRMI
examples.why: This title sits under the 'Optimasi beban kerja' heading, and the intro (entry 44) also uses 'beban kerja', so the English 'workload' here is inconsistent.

examples.source: Simulate 2D tilted-field Ising with the QESEM function
examples.translation: Simulasi Ising medan-miring 2D dengan fungsi QESEM
examples.suggested: Simulasikan Ising medan-miring 2D dengan fungsi QESEM
examples.why: The English is imperative, as is the next title (entry 59, 'Simulasikan model kicked Ising'). Using the noun form here makes adjacent titles inconsistent.

editor_note: None of the four rewritten entries (12, 30, 41, 61) would mislead a learner. The overwrite caveat in [30], the Pauli X/Y/Z explanation in [41] and the recommendation list in [61] all keep their meaning. Entry [12] has two small problems. "Blok utama" drops the "building" in "building blocks" ("blok pembangun utama" is the usual phrase). It also keeps "exponential kernel ... fungsi kernel klasikal", while the rewritten [41] says "fungsi kernel eksponensial klasik", so the same concept appears in two forms across the rewritten entries.

examples.source: The main building blocks of PQKs are reduced density matrices (RDMs)
examples.translation: Blok utama dari PQK adalah reduced density matrices (RDM)
examples.suggested: Blok pembangun utama PQK adalah reduced density matrices (RDM)
examples.why: "Blok utama" drops the idea of building blocks and reads flat. "Blok pembangun utama" is the natural Indonesian phrase, and "dari" is unnecessary here.

examples.source: a classical kernel function, such as an exponential kernel
examples.translation: fungsi kernel klasikal, seperti exponential kernel
examples.suggested: fungsi kernel klasik, seperti kernel eksponensial
examples.why: The rewritten entry [41] uses "fungsi kernel eksponensial klasik", but [12] keeps "exponential kernel" in English and uses "klasikal" instead of "klasik". The same concept should be rendered one way.

editor_note: The meaning of all three rewritten entries (33, 36, 55) matches the English. The 80/10/10 weighting, the "no direct couplings… when possible" caveat, and the list of what the plot does not show are all intact, so nothing here would mislead a learner. Two small things are left. First, the adjective "dynamic" switches between languages across the rewritten entries: "padanan semiklasik QFT+M dinamisnya" in [33], "Implementasi dynamic" in [36]. Second, "skor yang dibobotkan 80% terhadap error readout yang lebih rendah" in [36] follows the English "weighted toward" word for word and reads stiffly.

examples.source: The dynamic implementation does not require two-qubit gates
examples.translation: Implementasi dynamic tidak memerlukan two-qubit gate
examples.suggested: Implementasi dinamis tidak memerlukan two-qubit gate
examples.why: Entry 33, rewritten at the same time, uses 'dinamis' as the adjective. Mixing 'dynamic' and 'dinamis' for the same attribute is inconsistent. The term itself is still recognizable.

examples.source: using a score weighted 80% toward lower readout error and 10% each toward higher $T_1$ and $T_2$
examples.translation: menggunakan skor yang dibobotkan 80% terhadap error readout yang lebih rendah dan masing-masing 10% terhadap $T_1$ dan $T_2$ yang lebih tinggi
examples.suggested: menggunakan skor dengan bobot 80% untuk error readout yang lebih rendah serta masing-masing 10% untuk $T_1$ dan $T_2$ yang lebih tinggi
examples.why: 'dibobotkan ... terhadap' copies the English 'weighted toward'. 'dengan bobot ... untuk' is the more natural Indonesian phrasing.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally, with no drift in meaning. In entry 8, "most likely measurement outcome" becomes "hasil pengukuran dengan probabilitas tertinggi", "peaked at" becomes "terpusat pada", and "may no longer correspond" keeps its hedge as "mungkin tidak lagi bersesuaian". Entry 35 keeps the informal "kamu"-style register ("Pendapatmu").

All three rewritten entries (15, 36, 54) keep the English meaning. The heuristic-variational vs Trotter/time-evolution contrast, the "under suitable assumptions" caveat, the single-circuit vs set-of-circuits contrast and the top-20 plot are all intact, so nothing would mislead a learner. A native editor would still fix some phrasing. In [15], "Circuit semacam itu bisa dalam" is ambiguous, because "bisa dalam" reads as unfinished; "bisa memiliki kedalaman besar" is clearer. Also in [15], "dengan potensi jutaan suku interaksi" is a calque and should be "yang berpotensi memiliki jutaan suku interaksi". In [54], "Sampler primitive" keeps English word order where Indonesian needs "primitif Sampler", and "kamus counts" and the bare "diambil" for "sampled" read as stiff.

examples.source: Such circuits can be deep, which makes this approach better for applications to lattice models.
examples.translation: Circuit semacam itu bisa dalam, yang membuat pendekatan ini lebih cocok untuk aplikasi pada model kisi.
examples.suggested: Circuit semacam itu bisa memiliki kedalaman besar, sehingga pendekatan ini lebih cocok untuk model kisi.
examples.why: 'bisa dalam' is ambiguous and reads like an unfinished phrase. The technical sense (circuit depth) should be stated explicitly.

examples.source: which is appealing for chemistry Hamiltonians with potentially millions of interaction terms
examples.translation: yang menarik untuk Hamiltonian kimia dengan potensi jutaan suku interaksi
examples.suggested: yang menarik untuk Hamiltonian kimia yang berpotensi memiliki jutaan suku interaksi
examples.why: 'dengan potensi jutaan' is a calque of the English adverb; the verb form 'berpotensi memiliki' is the idiomatic Indonesian.

examples.source: After using the Sampler primitive to sample bitstrings from each circuit, we combine all of the results into a single counts dictionary and plot the top 20 most commonly sampled bitstrings.
examples.translation: Setelah menggunakan Sampler primitive untuk mengambil sampel bitstring dari setiap Circuit, kita menggabungkan semua hasil ke dalam satu kamus counts dan memplot 20 bitstring yang paling sering diambil.
examples.suggested: Setelah menggunakan primitif Sampler untuk mengambil sampel bitstring dari setiap Circuit, kita menggabungkan semua hasil ke dalam satu dictionary counts dan memplot 20 bitstring yang paling sering muncul dalam sampel.
examples.why: 'Sampler primitive' keeps English noun order, which Indonesian reverses. 'yang paling sering diambil' drops the sense of 'sampled'.

editor_note: None of the four rewritten entries (5, 6, 17, 53) would mislead a learner. Entry 17 is faithful, including the two-spinon continuum bounds and "Kedua batas ini ditampilkan sebagai kurva putus-putus". Entry 6 has several problems that make it inconsistent with the rest of the page. It uses "Anda" and the redundant "notebook Anda", while every other entry uses "kamu". It leaves "circuit" and "neutron-scattering" in English, where the page elsewhere uses "sirkuit" and "hamburan neutron". It also renders the template as "function template" rather than "templat fungsi". Entry 53 is accurate, but "Kita melalui empat langkah yang sama" is stiff, and "langkah-langkah berikutnya" is weaker than "later" ("langkah-langkah selanjutnya/akhir").

examples.source: can continue after you close your notebook
examples.translation: dapat terus berjalan setelah Anda menutup notebook Anda
examples.suggested: dapat terus berjalan setelah kamu menutup notebook
examples.why: Entry 6 uses 'Anda' but the rest of the page uses 'kamu', and the doubled possessive is a calque of the English.

examples.source: run the neutron-scattering experiment ... circuit construction
examples.translation: menjalankan eksperimen neutron-scattering ... konstruksi circuit
examples.suggested: menjalankan eksperimen hamburan neutron ... konstruksi sirkuit
examples.why: Elsewhere the page consistently uses 'hamburan neutron' and 'sirkuit', so leaving them in English here breaks consistency within the file.

examples.source: We walk through the same four steps as the simulator example
examples.translation: Kita melalui empat langkah yang sama seperti contoh simulator
examples.suggested: Kita akan menelusuri empat langkah yang sama seperti pada contoh simulator
examples.why: 'Kita melalui' reads as a stiff literal rendering of 'walk through'.

editor_note: Entry 7 keeps the English meaning: grid stability is a challenge, predicting stable conditions supports tool development, and the tutorial frames this as a classification task. Nothing in it would mislead a learner. The wording is not consistent with the rest of the page, though. It uses "kuantum" and "workflow", while entries 0-12 use "quantum" and "alur kerja". It also leaves "renewable" and "tools" in English, and "pembangkitan renewable yang variabel" reads like a calque, not how an Indonesian energy writer would put it.

examples.source: through a hybrid quantum–classical classification workflow
examples.translation: melalui workflow klasifikasi hybrid kuantum–klasik
examples.suggested: melalui alur kerja klasifikasi hybrid quantum–klasik
examples.why: The rest of the file uses 'quantum' (entries 0, 6, 8, 12) and 'alur kerja' (entries 1, 6, 9, 12). This entry switches to 'kuantum' and the English 'workflow'.

examples.source: integrate variable renewable generation and changing demand
examples.translation: mengintegrasikan pembangkitan renewable yang variabel dan permintaan yang berubah-ubah
examples.suggested: mengintegrasikan pembangkit energi terbarukan yang fluktuatif dan permintaan yang berubah-ubah
examples.why: 'Renewable' has a standard Indonesian equivalent, 'energi terbarukan'. 'Pembangkitan ... yang variabel' is a word-for-word calque of the English.

examples.source: support the development of tools for managing
examples.translation: mendukung pengembangan tools untuk mengelola
examples.suggested: mendukung pengembangan perangkat/alat untuk mengelola
examples.why: The English word 'tools' is left in running prose where a common Indonesian word exists.

editor_note: None of the 9 rewritten entries changes the meaning, and none would mislead a learner. The postselection-rate/fidelity reasoning in [63] and the tradeoff advice in [76] match the English. The problems are phrasing. In [14], two "yang" clauses in a row ("circuit yang didominasi Clifford yang berada di antara…") make it read as if the circuits, not the method, sit between error correction and mitigation. In [37], "estimasi fidelitas yang berjalan" copies "running estimate" word for word. [58] and [76] use the bare noun "Sampel"/"sampel" as an imperative verb, and [76] also has the calque "mendorong ke payload yang lebih besar".

examples.source: introduces a method for detecting logical errors in Clifford-dominated circuits that sits between full error correction and lighter-weight error mitigation
examples.translation: memperkenalkan metode untuk mendeteksi error logis dalam circuit yang didominasi Clifford yang berada di antara koreksi error penuh dan mitigasi error yang lebih ringan
examples.suggested: memperkenalkan metode—yang berada di antara koreksi error penuh dan mitigasi error yang lebih ringan—untuk mendeteksi error logis dalam circuit yang didominasi Clifford
examples.why: The two stacked 'yang' clauses let 'berada di antara' attach to 'circuit' rather than to 'metode'. The sentence becomes ambiguous about what sits between error correction and mitigation.

examples.source: and `cum_mean_sem` tracks the running fidelity estimate
examples.translation: dan `cum_mean_sem` melacak estimasi fidelitas yang berjalan
examples.suggested: dan `cum_mean_sem` melacak estimasi fidelitas kumulatif
examples.why: 'yang berjalan' copies 'running' word for word. Here the meaning is a cumulative estimate, which 'kumulatif' expresses naturally.

examples.source: Sample the bare payload and the checked circuits with Qiskit Aer.
examples.translation: Sampel payload polos dan circuit yang telah dicheck dengan Qiskit Aer.
examples.suggested: Ambil sampel dari payload polos dan circuit yang telah diberi check menggunakan Qiskit Aer.
examples.why: 'Sampel' is a noun and does not work as an imperative verb. 'dicheck' is an awkward English-Indonesian hybrid. [76] has the same problem with 'sampel lebih banyak stabilizer'.

examples.source: to push to larger payloads, scale the shot budget with the inverse of the postselection rate
examples.translation: untuk mendorong ke payload yang lebih besar, skalakan budget shot dengan kebalikan laju postselection
examples.suggested: untuk beralih ke payload yang lebih besar, skalakan budget shot sebanding dengan kebalikan laju postselection
examples.why: 'mendorong ke' copies 'push to' word for word and reads stiffly in Indonesian technical prose.

editor_note: All three rewritten entries (7, 41, 47) keep the English meaning, with no drift or invented claims. Entry 7 translates the Fire Opal paragraph faithfully, with "penekanan error", "dekoherensi" and "fidelitas lebih tinggi". Entry 47 has two small wording slips. "raw counts" becomes "Jumlah mentah", which reads as "raw sum/total" rather than measurement counts. "with an arbitrary choice of 4096 shots" becomes the calque "dengan pilihan arbitrer $4096$ shot", which a native technical editor would rephrase. "dimensi ikatan" for bond dimension is correct.

examples.source: The raw counts are normalized
examples.translation: Jumlah mentah dinormalisasi
examples.suggested: Hasil hitungan (counts) mentah dinormalisasi
examples.why: 'Jumlah' means sum or total, so 'jumlah mentah' suggests a single raw total rather than the per-bitstring measurement counts. It is still recognizable from context, but imprecise.

examples.source: with an arbitrary choice of $4096$ shots
examples.translation: dengan pilihan arbitrer $4096$ shot
examples.suggested: dengan $4096$ shot (jumlah yang dipilih secara arbitrer)
examples.why: This copies the English noun phrase word for word and reads stiffly in Indonesian. The meaning is preserved.
